Subject: Follow-up: VPC connectivity and networking questions

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — really helpful. A quick summary from our side and a few follow-ups we need to qualify the integration: 

- Connectivity model: Acme prefers private connectivity. We need to understand the options you support (VPC endpoints, IP allowlists, NAT/egress, and whether you support private link-like endpoints).
- DNS & discovery: How will requests from our services resolve Redwood endpoints? Can we keep traffic on our VPC and avoid public egress?
- mTLS and auth: We need details on mutual TLS support (client certs from our side), and how that interacts with SDK auth (API keys / short-lived tokens).
- Embeddings/reranker: If we push embeddings to Redwood, how is data segmented? Any special routing or extra network considerations for vector uploads?
- Structured output / tool calling: Will function/tool calls require additional inbound connections (webhooks) from Redwood, or are those always outgoing from our side?

Can you please send: (1) a short network diagram and allowlist IPs, (2) a recommended setup for DNS/egress, and (3) an estimate for how long the private connectivity setup typically takes? Also copying our infra alias (it-infra@acme-corp.com) — they'd like to loop in their security folks after we get the details.

Thanks,
Alice

--
Alice Tsing
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Corp

Hi Alice — great to connect, and thanks for the clear list. Attaching our concise VPC setup guide and a starter mutual action plan (MAP). Jonas (solutions engineering) and Aditya (product infra) are looped in to confirm the technical specifics below.

Quick answers / next steps:
- Attachments: redwood-vpc-setup-guide.pdf + acme-mutual-action-plan.xlsx attached.
- IP allowlist: we'll provide the exact Egress/Ingress CIDR ranges Jonas lists below; those cover our hosted and dedicated endpoints.
- VPC endpoints: we support private endpoints for Dedicated/Private deployments. For Hosted API customers we offer egress-to-Redwood via peering and static outbound IP ranges (allowlist).
- mTLS: Supported on Private deployments and VPC endpoints. For Hosted we can do TLS + client auth using customer-managed certs on Dedicated only — Jonas will confirm details.
- DNS: Recommend configuring conditional forwarding to our private DNS zone (details in the guide).
- Embeddings & routing: embeddings uploads are over TLS to the same endpoints; vector storage is scoped per account/tenant and we can keep that traffic over the private connectivity path.

Proposed immediate actions:
1) Jonas to send exact IPs/CIDRs, DNS guidance, and a short network diagram (today).
2) We’ll create a HubSpot MAP with milestones + dependencies (I attached the MAP).
3) If you want, we can schedule a 30-min call next week to walk through the VPC design with your infra team.

Jonas — can you confirm IP ranges and the recommended mTLS flow?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: VPC connectivity and networking questions

Hi all — technical follow-up from my side with the specifics requested. See inline and attached network diagram.

1) IP ranges / allowlist (Hosted API static outbound ranges)
- Primary egress CIDRs (US): 34.219.128.0/20, 54.183.0.0/18, 3.216.0.0/14
- Health/management IPs (short list for control plane callbacks): 54.201.33.10, 54.201.33.11

If you go with Redwood Dedicated or Private we provide VPC endpoint instructions (VPC peering / PrivateLink depending on cloud) and you do not need to allow the public ranges above.

2) DNS / discovery
- Recommended: conditional forwarding of your private DNS zone (*.redwood.internal) to our resolver IPs (see guide). This keeps all name resolution internal and avoids public DNS leaks.
- Alternate: use PrivateLink + private DNS entries injected into your VPC (works on AWS/Azure equivalents).

3) mTLS & auth
- Private deployment: full mTLS supported. We accept customer client certs; we can also rotate server certs via your KMS if desired.
- Hosted: standard TLS with API keys or short-lived OAuth tokens is the default. We can negotiate client certs for Dedicated customers on a per-contract basis.
- SDK auth: the Redwood SDK supports API keys, OAuth short-lived tokens, and can be configured to present a client cert when running inside a Private deployment. No SDK changes are required for structured output or tool calling flows.

4) Embeddings / reranker
- Embeddings ingestion uses the same secure endpoint and follows the same routing rules. Data is stored scoped to your account; for Dedicated/Private we can isolate storage to your tenant and keep traffic entirely within your VPC. Reranking services call into the same vector store — no additional inbound holes required.

5) Tool calling / webhooks
- By default function/tool calls are executed by Redwood and callbacks/webhooks are outgoing to your configured endpoints. If you require webhook endpoints to be reachable from Redwood, we can provide an outbound list (above) or configure a proxy inside your VPC to pull results.

6) Typical timeline
- Hosted (allowlist path): 1-3 business days after allowlist + DNS config.
- Dedicated/Private (endpoint + peering): 2-4 weeks depending on procurement and network scheduling.

7) Next steps / deliverables (action items)
- Jonas: share network-diagram.png and final CIDRs (attached).
- Marissa: send MAP and contract steps to procurement.
- Acme infra: confirm whether you prefer Hosted with allowlist or Dedicated Private endpoint so we can prioritize docs and SOW items.

Code snippet (SDK usage with mTLS flag - sample):
```
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key="<REDACTED>", mTLS_cert_path="/etc/ssl/client.pem")
resp = client.chat.create(model="rwd-3b", input="Summarize the infra doc")
```
Attachment: network-diagram.png

Happy to hop on a call this week if helpful.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
